title: VIX curve inversion as a de-risk trigger
ask: Is VIX curve inversion a better de-risk trigger?
reason: No. Sharpe 1.24 to 1.12, and turnover tripled.
hypothesis: Front-month VIX futures above the second month is a better de-risk signal than SPY's trend and volatility.
question: Would cutting exposure when the VIX futures curve inverts, alone or alongside the current rule, improve the live book?
prior: An inverted curve means the market is pricing near-term stress, and it is observable every day. It might react faster than a 200-day average.
citations: Cheng, I.-H. (2019). The VIX Premium. Review of Financial Studies 32(1).
method: Our own VIX futures curve, built from Cboe's daily settlements and checked against VIXY.
The deployed book at its live settings with only the trigger swapped: inversion alone, or either rule.
Pass needs all four: Sharpe up, worst drawdown no worse, every crisis window within 1 point, overlay turnover up at most 25%.
verdict_reason: Both versions failed. Inversion alone lowered Sharpe from 1.24 to 1.12, the either-rule version to 1.10, and overlay turnover roughly tripled. The curve flips back and forth around every spike, so the trigger cut exposure late and restored it during rebounds. Archived.
lessons: A signal that switches within days needs to be checked for turnover, not only for Sharpe.
